Bards.description_wikitext:
Bards includes all performers. See specific sub-categories for: 

* [[:Category:Musicians|Musicians]] - tag bards as Musicians if their page can cite at least three recordings of musical performance and/or original musical works.
** [[:Category:Singers|Singers]] - tag bards as Singers if their page can cite at least three recordings of their singing.
** [[:Category:Instrumentalists|Instrumentalists]] - tag bards as Instrumentalists if their page can cite at least three recordings of playing instruments. 
** [[:Category:Songwriters|Songwriters]] - tag bards as Songwriters if their page can cite at least three songs they have written.
* [[:Category:Storytellers|Storytellers]] - tag bards as Storytellers if their page can cite at least three recordings of storytelling performance and/or original stories.
* [[:Category:Jesters|Jesters]] - use for comics, fools, jokers, etc; tag bards as Jesters if their page can cite at least three comedic performances.
* [[:Category:Poets|Poets]] - tag bards as Poets if their page can cite at least three recordings of poetic performance and/or original poems.
* [[:Category:Dancers|Dancers]] - tag bards as Dancers if their page can cite at least three dance performance recordings and/or dance instruction articles.

It is acceptable (and encouraged) to create a page that does not ''yet'' contain three citations, and allow others to add more citations later. If you find a page that does not contain three citations, first try searching the web to see if additional citations can be added to the page. Only de-list a page from a category if it seems that three citations do not exist. '''All citations must be hosted elsewhere''' and linked to here.

[[Category:Top_Level_Categories]]
Bards.name: Bards

'''Recording & performance of these works can be fraught, because they are usually under copyright, and performers/creators/musicians outside the bardic community often have less permissive views about community members using their work'''.

[[Category:Source Category]]

Comedic.description_wikitext:
The wiki uses a limited number of mood tags to help ensure work is findable and the tag system remains manageable. The intent of a 'mood' tag is to help bards find repertoire that will work in a particular context: a performer at a party or a bar may be seeking happy or funny pieces and wishing to avoid tragic pieces, while a performer at a funeral may have the opposite preference. A song's mood does not have to be perfectly captured by the tag, so long as it would be appropriate to perform in similar contexts to the other songs in the tag.

Comedic should be used for pieces that are comic, humorous, silly, parodies, lighthearted or otherwise suitable for the lightening of moods (and unsuitable for serious occasions).

See all [[:Category:Moods|Moods]] or read more at [[Categories]].
[[Category:Moods]]
Comedic.name: Comedic

Contrafacta.description_wikitext:
Contrafacta is the source category for pieces that set new words to historical/folk/traditional tunes - also called "parody", "filk", "lyrical adaptation", "rewrite" and so on. 

You may also categorise these pieces as [[:Category:Pre-1600 Sources|Pre-1600 Sources]] (for documentably pre-1600 melodies) or [[:Category:Traditional & Folk|Traditional & Folk]] (for folk tunes), and may categorise them as [[:Category:SCA Pieces|SCA Pieces]] or [[:Category:SF&F Pieces|SF&F Pieces]] if the new words were written by SCA or SF&F-related artists. 

If the piece sets new words to an existing modern tune that is under copyright, use [[:Category:Contrafacta (Modern)|Contrafacta (Modern)]] instead.

If the piece sets existing historical words to a new tune, it belongs in [[:Category:Setting Pieces|Setting Pieces]].

[[Category:Source Category]]
Contrafacta.name: Contrafacta

pages.title: When A Knight Won His Spurs (SCA Version)

Contrafacta (Modern).description_wikitext:
This category is for pieces which put new words to the tune of an existing song where the copyright for the song belongs to somebody else. '''The legal situation for recording or performing such songs can be fraught.'''

See [[Categories]] for more information about how works are categorised on Bardic Torch. See [[:Category:Contrafacta|Contrafacta]] for pieces where the tune is historical/folk/traditional. 

Contrafacta (singular contrafactum) are also known as parodies, filk, adaptations and rewrites. We use the term contrafacta at BardicTorch because it is clear and unambiguous, whereas 'filk' is sometimes used to refer to all SF&F music or the entire 'nerd folk' community.

[[Category:Source Category]]
Contrafacta (Modern).name: Contrafacta (Modern)

Moods.description_wikitext:
The intent of a 'mood' tag is to help bards find repertoire that will work in a particular context: a performer at a party or a bar may be seeking happy or funny pieces and wishing to avoid tragic pieces, while a performer at a funeral may have the opposite preference. A song's mood does not have to be perfectly captured by the tag, so long as it would be appropriate to perform in similar contexts to the other songs in the tag. 

Try to use one of the broad categories listed in [[Categories]] as a piece's mood in its infobox.

It is possible to create more specific categories, which should be listed here by tagging the category page with <nowiki>[[Category:Moods]]</nowiki>, but remember that the 'mood' tag is intended to help bards find pieces appropriate for a particular '''context or situation'''. We do not intend to split the 'Joyful' tag into 'Excited', 'Happy', 'Cheerful' or other extremely subjective sub-categories. You might, however, create a new category under 'Warlike' for songs suitable as marching songs, or a new category under 'Tragic' for songs specifically suitable at funerals/rememberances, or a new category under 'Romantic' for songs appropriate at weddings.

[[Category:Top Level Categories]]
Moods.name: Moods

SCA Pieces.description_wikitext:
Bardic Torch uses a set number of 'Source Categories' to categorise the origins of pieces. Please use 'SCA Pieces' for pieces entirely written by bards performing in an SCA context.

Do not use for any and all pieces performed in the SCA - only those entirely written by members of the SCA for performance in the SCA. 

* Songs found in historical sources pre-1600 should be categorised as [[:Category:Pre-1600 Sources|Pre-1600 Sources]]. 
* Songs sung in the SCA, but which originate as traditional (out-of-copyright or unknown-author) folk tunes, should be categorised as [[:Category:Traditional Folk Music|Traditional/Folk Music]]. 
* Songs created by modern authors who are '''not''' part of the bardic tradition should be categorised as [[:Category:Borrowings|Borrowings]]. Be especially careful of copyright with these pieces. 
* If a bard is associated with the SCA, but the piece was written for SF&F spaces such as fan conventions, use [[:Category:SF and F Pieces|SF&F Pieces]].
* If an SCA bard sets new words to a historical tune, use [[:Category:Contrafacta|Contrafacta]].
* If an SCA bard sets historical words to a new tune, use [[:Category:SettingPieces|Setting Pieces]]. 
For more information, see [[Categories]].

[[Category:Source Category]]
SCA Pieces.name: SCA Pieces

The intent of a 'mood' tag is to help bards find repertoire that will work in a particular context: a performer at a party or a bar may be seeking happy or funny pieces and wishing to avoid tragic pieces, while a performer at a funeral may have the opposite preference. Story (Mood).description_wikitext:
This mood tag is used for pieces that are too complex to categorise into a single [[Category:Moods|Mood]] tag, because they contain a plot.

For example, a song where a young squire strives to become a knight might be [[:Category:Warlike|Warlike]], a song where the squire celebrates becoming knighted might be [[:Category:Joyful|Joyful]], and a song where the knight dies might be [[:Category:Tragic|Tragic]]. If a song follows the entire journey from the young squire's first battle to the old knight's eventual death, it should not be categorised with all three moods; instead, it belongs here.

The intent of a 'mood' tag is to help bards find repertoire that will work in a particular context: a performer at a party or a bar may be seeking happy or funny pieces and wishing to avoid tragic pieces, while a performer at a funeral may have the opposite preference. A song's mood does not have to be perfectly captured by the tag, so long as it would be appropriate to perform in similar contexts to the other songs in the tag.

This page collects all the top-level categories for pieces (not for bards) on Bardic Torch, for ease of navigation.

See [[Categories]] for more information about how to use categories.
Top Level Categories.name: Top Level Categories

Topics.description_wikitext:
See [[Categories]] for more information about how topic tags should be used.

Use broad topics in the 'topic' section of a piece's infobox. Create subcategories wherever possible for more specific topics. For example:
* 'Swords', 'Fighting', 'Shieldwalls' or 'Battles' should all be subcategories of 'War' - not top-level categories.
* Topics such as 'Plants', 'Animals', 'Wildlife' or 'Forests' should be subcategories of 'Nature'.
* Topics such as 'Travel', 'Wanderlust', 'Exploration' or 'Sailing' should be subcategories of 'Wandering'.
* Topics such as 'Magic', 'Elves' or 'Mythical Creatures' should be subcategories of 'Supernatural'
* Topics such as 'Honour', 'Chivalry' or 'Praise Songs' should be subcategories of 'Virtues'

Notes on how to use topics:
* [[:Category:Patriotic|Patriotic]] - Use subcategories in brackets for the particular nation, kingdom or group being celebrated, eg. [[:Category:Patriotic (Atlantia)|Patriotic (Atlantia)]]
* [[:Category:Bardic Meta|Bardic Meta]] - use for songs about singing, stories about storytellers or poems about poetry 
* [[:Category:SCA (Topic)|SCA (Topic)]] - use for songs about the SCA - including its peerages, history, events, community, regalia, etc.
* [[:Category:Identity|Identity]] - use for songs about diversity, inclusion, belonging and pride for marginalised identities. 
* [[:Category:Historical People & Events|Historical People & Events]] - use for songs written about historical events and people 'by modern authors' - particularly songs aiming to educate about history.

When you create a new topic, ensure you add the [[:Category:Topics|Topics]] category to the category page. This will ensure the topic is added to the list of topics.

[[Category:Top Level Categories]]
Topics.name: Topics

Traditional & Folk.description_wikitext:
Source categories on BardicTorch help to keep track of which works come from historically documentable sources, which were written by members of SCA / re-enactment / LARP communities, which originated in SF&F, which came from folk music, and so on. Please see [[Categories]] for more information. 

Use "Traditional & Folk" for pieces that are not documentably pre-1600, but are old enough to not be copyrightable (or do not have a known author). Do not use for pieces protected by copyright, even if they are in the folk 'genre'; use [[:Category:Borrowings|Borrowings]] for pieces by modern professional folk artists outside the bardic community.

[[Category:Source Category]]
Traditional & Folk.name: Traditional & Folk

Trimaris.description_wikitext:
Trimaris is the [[:Category:SCA Kingdom|SCA Kingdom]] that covers most of Florida. 

This page is for bards from Trimaris. Use [[:Category:Patriotic (Trimaris)|Patriotic (Trimaris)]] for Trimarian anthems.

[[Category:SCA Kingdom]]
Trimaris.name: Trimaris

True Events.description_wikitext:
Use this category for tales that are said to have really happened to bards and their friends in modern nerd-dom. Do not use it for historical events; this is to maintain a distinction between tales of real events before 1600 vs. "No Shit There I Was" stories. 

See [[Categories]] for more.

[[Category:Top Level Categories]]

Warlike.description_wikitext:
Warlike should be used for pieces that are suitable for performance on a re-enactment battlefield or in relation to martial arts activities; often these will be war-related, angry, determined, fierce or upbeat.

Mood tags on Bardic Torch are used to help bards select appropriate works for a particular context. Warlike pieces do not necessarily need to be about war; they could be any pieces suitable for performing before battle to hype up fighters, or similar contexts.

See all [[:Category:Moods|Moods]] or read more at [[Categories]].
[[Category:Moods]]
Warlike.name: Warlike

Welsh.description_wikitext:
This category is not necessarily for works from Wales - it could be any pieces suitable for Welsh personas in the SCA, for re-enactors focused on Wales, LARPs in settings inspired by Wales, or Wales-themed events.

When adding new culture categories, ensure you add <nowiki>[[Category:Cultures]]</nowiki> to the category page so that they are correctly listed under [[:Category:Cultures|Cultures]].

West Kingdom.description_wikitext:
The [https://westkingdom.org/ West Kingdom] is the oldest kingdom in the SCA. It covers Northern California, Nevada, Alaska, Japan, Korea and Thailand.

This page is for bards from, or associated with, the West Kingdom. Use [[:Category:Patriotic (West Kingdom)|Patriotic (West Kingdom)]] for anthems of the West. 

[[:Category:SCA Kingdom|Click to see other SCA Kingdoms]].

[[Category:SCA Kingdom]]
West Kingdom.name: West Kingdom

Women's Songs.description_wikitext:
This is a subcategory of [[:Category:Identity|Identity]]. See [[:Category:Topics|Topics]] for all topics. 

Use for pieces celebrating women's inclusion, feminism, women's achievements or women's history. Do not use this category for any/every song containing a woman; this is for the 'girl power' songs.

See [[Categories]] for more information.

[[Category:Identity]]
Women's Songs.name: Women's Songs
